content:
Ready for a full Class 5 Maths Olympiad rehearsal? A real IMO or SOF paper mixes every chapter — large numbers, factors, fractions, decimals, percentage, measurement, geometry, mensuration, temperature, money and data handling — in one 30-question set. This free test gives a 10-question taste, and the practice-papers e-book gives you 25 complete Maths Olympiad Class 5 sample papers with answers.

What a Class 5 IMO sample paper looks like

  • 30 questions in one paper, balanced across all 11 chapters
  • A mix of number work, fractions, decimals, percentage, mensuration, temperature and data
  • An answer key and step-by-step solution for every question
  • Graded intermediate to hard, just like the real SOF Olympiad

How to use Class 5 Olympiad practice papers

  • Sit one paper in a quiet 30–40 minute slot, no help
  • Mark it with the answer key, then read the solution for every wrong one
  • Note which chapter the mistakes cluster in and revise that chapter
  • Repeat weekly — steady practice beats last-minute cramming

Take the free mixed test

The 10 questions below are pulled from across the syllabus. The full 25 Practice Papers e-book has 750 questions — 25 papers of 30 — each fully solved, with colourful diagrams wherever they help: the best Maths Olympiad class 5 question papers PDF for exam practice.

Learn the syllabus first with the free IMO Maths Olympiad course at vidaara.org.

questions.explanation: Line up the digits by place and add with carrying: 60,58,349 + 19,46,758 = 80,05,107.

questions.q: Find the smallest digit that can fill the blank so that 27_4 is divisible by 6.
questions.explanation: The number must be even and have a digit sum divisible by 3. With 2, the number 2724 is even and its digit sum 15 is a multiple of 3.

questions.q: Riya had Rs 240. She spent 1/3 of it on a book and then 1/4 of the remaining money on a pen. How much money is left with her?
questions.explanation: First step: 1/3 of 240 is used, so 240 − 80 = 160 remain. Second step: 1/4 of 160 = 40 is used, leaving 160 − 40 = 120.

questions.q: A regular nonagon (9 equal sides) has a perimeter of 108 cm. Find one side.
questions.explanation: All 9 sides of a regular nonagon are equal, so each side = 108 ÷ 9 = 12 cm.
